solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Uni mobs wrecked vehicle

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so its letters are broken apart and rebuilt

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Rioting university students smash up a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Uni is British shorthand for university, so the surface pictures a student riot; the vehicle they wreck is the answer made of their own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the old full name for a bus, a public passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Annoyingly slow empty boat in river

indicators.note: the boat's remains go in the river

parts.note: the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and another in East Anglia

indicators.note: an emptied word has its inside taken out, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: BOAT with its middle letters OA removed

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a sluggish, unladen boat on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is one of the commonest crossword rivers, and 'empty' is a standard instruction to keep only the outer letters of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, the irritating kind of dimness that fails to see a point.

clue.text: Exclusive new school in the East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their H's

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
HARROW, the English public school, with the H dropped

explanation.surface: A smart new private school opening in the poorer East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English boarding school; the East End Cockney accent drops the initial H, which crosswords use to delete an H.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow and exclusive both describe something restricted to a few, as in a narrow or exclusive circle.

clue.text: School chief supporting check for dope

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath

parts.note: to check is to block or stop
the head teacher

explanation.surface: A headmistress backing a drugs test at her school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check for dope' reads as a drugs test, but dope is the person, not the drug. In a down clue 'supporting' puts the first-named piece underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and so is a blockhead, someone with a head as dense as wood.

clue.text: Go and shop as cheaply as possible

definitions.meaning: a British euphemism for going to the lavatory
literally, part with the smallest coin there is

explanation.surface: Advice to hit the shops but spend as little as you can.
explanation.walkthrough: British public toilets once had coin locks costing one old penny, so 'spend a penny' became the polite phrase for going to the loo.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to urinate, which is what 'go' means in the nursery sense.

clue.text: One hour trapped in crash after motorway confusion

indicators.note: the hour is caught inside the crash

parts.note: M for motorway, as in the M1
I is the Roman numeral one
a smash is a crash
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A pile-up on the motorway leaves someone stuck for an hour in the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside SMASH to make SHMASH, and M and I stand in front. The blog reads MI together as the M1 motorway, which gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble of things.

clue.text: Witty remark about a ditch full of water

indicators.note: the witty remark goes around the A

parts.note: a mot (bon mot) is a witty saying
A is used as itself

explanation.surface: A clever quip made about some waterlogged ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is borrowed from French bon mot, a witty remark, and it turns up often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a deep ditch filled with water, dug round a castle.

clue.text: Quality of arrows left to kill seabirds aboard ship

parts.note: SS, steamship
L is the abbreviation for left
to end a life is to kill
ernes are sea eagles

explanation.surface: An archery quality turned into a scene of shooting seabirds from a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests arrows being used to kill seabirds, but the arrows belong to the definition and the killing is just END.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an arrow's shaft is long and thin, so thinness is the quality the clue picks out.

clue.text: A manic hello changed sad mood

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: Someone's frantic greeting gives way to gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a swing from mania to depression, which is the very condition the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Melancholia is deep, lasting sadness, an old name for depression.

clue.text: Intermittent springs mostly come up around unfinished dig

indicators.note: most of COME, losing its last letter

parts.note: spas are mineral springs

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top
DIG without its final letter

parts.note: COM(e) turned upside down
DIG with the G cut off

explanation.surface: Springs that bubble up now and then around an abandoned dig site.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a geyser, and 'springs' is really the resort word SPAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means happening in fits and starts, which is what intermittent means.

clue.text: Cowboy gets all Uruguayan calves herded once at the front

indicators.note: take the letter at the front of each word

parts.words: gets all Uruguayan calves herded once
parts.note: first letters of gets, all, Uruguayan, calves, herded, once

explanation.surface: A South American cowboy rounding up calves in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a picture of the answer at work: gauchos herded cattle on the Uruguayan and Argentine plains.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a cowboy of the South American pampas.

clue.text: Girl assistant carrying hamper that's short

indicators.note: DELAY cut short loses its last letter
the assistant carries the hamper inside

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
DELAY, to hamper, missing its Y

explanation.surface: A young helper lugging a picnic hamper that is too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket but is the verb, to hinder.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is a girl's name, as well as a city.

clue.text: What's in Yangtze river plant raised for local animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written upwards

parts.note: the Yangtze is a Chinese river, so what it holds is Chinese water
REED, a waterside plant, turned upside down

explanation.surface: A riverside plant being grown to feed an animal that lives nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' refers back to the Yangtze: the animal is local to China, so the definition only makes sense once the river is read as Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese water deer is a small tusked deer native to the reed beds of the Yangtze.

clue.text: High on Everest, maybe when there's less demand

definitions.meaning: read cryptically: off (high, as meat going bad) plus peak (Everest, for example)
the fares and electricity rates at quiet times

explanation.surface: A climber high on Everest, perhaps in the quiet season.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits: meat that is high has gone off, and Everest is a peak, so OFF plus PEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak describes times such as late evening when fewer people travel or use power, so demand is lower.

clue.text: Pastry again taken before tea? Try something different

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in order before the tea

parts.note: a turnover is a folded pastry with a filling
anew = again
tea leaf, the dried leaf that tea is made from

explanation.surface: A second pastry eaten ahead of teatime, with a suggestion to vary the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all afternoon tea, and 'tea' is not the meal but the plant's leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn over a new leaf is to start behaving differently, begin afresh.

clue.text: Deliverance when umpire accepts position

indicators.note: the umpire takes the position inside him

parts.note: ref, short for referee, an umpire
the lie of the land, how something is positioned

explanation.surface: The relief felt when an umpire agrees with a player's stance.
explanation.walkthrough: LIE as position is the golfer's sense, the way a ball lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is deliverance, rescue from distress or danger.

clue.text: Strangely inured accepting V&A is never changing

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a strange new way
the fodder takes V and A into its letters

parts.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

explanation.surface: Someone oddly used to the V&A museum, which never alters its displays.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum of art and design in London; the ampersand is dropped and V and A join the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvaried means remaining the same throughout, never changing.

clue.text: What encloses cattle a deer half avoided

parts.note: livestock, farm animals
A is used as itself
DEER with its second half dropped

explanation.surface: A fence around a herd that a deer only half manages to dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What encloses cattle' looks like the whole definition, but cattle is wordplay for STOCK and the definition stops at 'What encloses'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a fence of stakes built to enclose and protect a space.

clue.text: God of old Babel

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a babel is a noisy confusion of voices, a din

explanation.surface: A deity of the ancient city of Babel.
explanation.walkthrough: Babel looks like the biblical tower, which suggests a Middle Eastern god, but here it is just a noun for noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology, who gives his name to Wednesday.

clue.text: Element of humanity and ecstasy includes God mostly

indicators.note: most of GANESH, losing its last letter

parts.note: man = humankind
E, slang for the drug ecstasy
GANESH, the elephant-headed Hindu god, without his H

explanation.surface: Humanity and ecstasy containing a trace of the divine.
explanation.walkthrough: The god sits between MAN and E. Ganesh (also Ganesha) is the Hindu god of beginnings, pictured with an elephant's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a metallic chemical element, number 25.

clue.text: Closure date of disused railway

parts.note: dead = no longer in use
a railway line

explanation.surface: The date an old railway was shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a railway closure, and read literally a disused railway is a dead line.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is the date by which something must be finished and closed off.

clue.text: Period of king holding power certainly forgotten

indicators.note: the king holds the other pieces inside him

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's king
P is the symbol for power
yea, an old word for yes or certainly

explanation.surface: A king's reign when his power was surely forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgotten' marks YEA as a word that has fallen out of use, the archaic form of yes; it says nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap year is a period of 366 days, with an extra day added in February.

clue.text: Bit of help to net fish then hunt game

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of help
the ide, a freshwater fish
and = then, next
to seek is to hunt for

explanation.surface: A helper catching fish and then going off hunting game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt game' reads as shooting wild animals, but game is the definition and hunt is SEEK. The IDE is a crossword regular among fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide-and-seek is the children's game in which one player hunts for the others.

clue.text: Heavily-built rodent eating southeastern monkey

parts.note: the marmot, a large stout ground squirrel
SE, south-east

explanation.surface: A stocky rodent eating a monkey from the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavily-built' is there to pick out the marmot among rodents; it is part of the wordplay, not a description of the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: Spoil lie about report with alien which contains rubbish

parts.note: to waste is to spoil or squander
a paper is a written report
to bask is to lie about in the sun
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Wrecking a report that lies about an alien, one full of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken out of clue order, report before lie. 'Rubbish' sounds like a verdict on the report but is litter, and 'lie' is lounging, not lying.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the office bin exists to hold discarded paper and other litter.

clue.text: Left cheated, taken in by a gang

parts.note: A is used as itself

indicators.note: the word for cheated is taken inside the gang

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
done = swindled, as in 'I've been done'

explanation.surface: A victim left swindled after being taken in by a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' doubles in the surface as fooled, which fits the cheating, but here it is only the container signal. Done for cheated is informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means left behind, deserted.

clue.text: Catholic city with the French court in charge

parts.note: EC, the postcode of the City of London
le is French for the
Ct is the abbreviation for court
i/c, in charge

explanation.surface: A Catholic city whose French court is in control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' with a capital pretends to be the church; it is the lower-case sense, wide-ranging. EC is the City of London's postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic tastes are broad and varied, and eclectic means drawing on a wide range of sources.

clue.text: Stray scent almost enveloping one

indicators.note: WAFT loses its last letter
to envelop is to wrap round, so the shortened scent wraps round the one

parts.note: WAFT, a drifting smell, without the T
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A faint scent drifting round a lost creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like a lost pet but is a homeless child here.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a stray, a homeless and neglected child or animal.

clue.text: I finish cutting mullet? Horrendous

parts.note: a mullet is a fish
I is used as itself
end = finish

explanation.surface: Someone finishes chopping a mullet and finds the result dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mullet' may suggest the haircut, which a cutting could be about; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish means devilishly cruel or dreadful, like a fiend.

clue.text: Caught poem's secret message

parts.note: c, caught, in cricket scoring
an ode is a poem; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A poem that has been caught carrying a hidden message.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards, where a batsman out caught is marked c.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a system for sending secret messages, and by extension the message itself.

clue.text: Mystic briefly shaped revolutionary branch of philosophy

indicators.note: SHAPED is cut short, losing its D
the letters are turned over into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
SHAPED with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A mystic who briefly shaped a radical new school of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' looks as if it trims 'Mystic', but trimming MYSTIC leaves the C short; it is SHAPED that loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy dealing with being, reality and first principles.

clue.text: Role needing quiet skill

indicators.note: the quiet letter needs the skill to follow it

parts.note: p, piano, quiet in music
art = skill

explanation.surface: An acting role that calls for subtle skill.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the musical marking piano, meaning play quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the theatre: an actor is cast in a role, or given a part.

clue.text: Choir ceased performing in area of York Minster?

indicators.note: the letters perform, putting on a new arrangement

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: The choir stopped singing somewhere inside York Minster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area of York Minster' suggests the nave or choir stalls, but it is the whole region the minster governs; the question mark flags that the minster stands for its archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: York Minster is the seat of the Archbishop of York, and the area under an archbishop is an archdiocese.

clue.text: What could make Clare go away

parts.note: the setter's reading: CLEAR, knocked off (anagrammed), makes CLARE
the straight definition

explanation.surface: Something that might persuade Clare to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, CLEAR with 'off' as an anagram signal, and its letters rearrange into CLARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear off is a brusque British way of telling someone to go away.

clue.text: What overseer does is very mean

parts.note: super = very, extremely, as in super-rich
to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A complaint that a supervisor's work is terribly stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very mean' reads as miserly, but mean is the verb, to intend.
explanation.definitionFit: To superintend is to oversee, which is exactly what an overseer does.

clue.text: Beginning to notice terribly serious mental condition

indicators.note: SERIOUS is terribly mangled into a new order
the beginning of notice is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of notice
SERIOUS rearranged

explanation.surface: Starting to spot a grave disorder of the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly serious' reads as a single phrase for very grave, but terribly is the anagram signal for SERIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental condition marked by anxiety or obsessive behaviour.

clue.text: Deployed armadas line sea port

indicators.note: the letters are deployed, spread out into a new formation

parts.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
L is the abbreviation for line
anagram fodder, 3 letters

explanation.surface: Fleets are sent out to line up off a seaport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea port' reads as one phrase, but sea joins the anagram and port alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dar es Salaam is the chief port and largest city of Tanzania.

clue.text: Get over with a leap and bound sober

parts.note: a jumper clears a fence
bound for = headed for

explanation.surface: An athlete vaulting a barrier and springing away, stone-cold sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' sits beside 'leap' as another jump, but here it means heading for somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear-headed means thinking clearly, not muddled by drink.

clue.text: Subdued glow has the ability to enchant surrounding loch

parts.note: can = is able
to delight is to enchant
L is the abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A soft light with the power to charm the area around a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: L for loch (lake) is a map abbreviation used in Scottish place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlelight is the soft, low glow given off by candles.

clue.text: Pragmatic statesman's approach putting true pressure on drunk held by lout

indicators.note: the pieces are put together in order
the word for drunk is held inside the lout
in a down clue, on means placed above what follows

parts.note: real = true
P is the symbol for pressure
oik, British slang for a lout
lit (up) = drunk

explanation.surface: A statesman's method of leaning on a drunken yob who is being restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: OIK is British slang for an uncouth, loutish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Realpolitik is politics driven by practical power interests rather than ideals.

clue.text: Section of pretty pertinent class

indicators.note: the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

parts.note: the last two letters of pretty and the first two of pertinent

explanation.surface: Part of a class that is rather relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' reads as rather, qualifying pertinent, but it is only there for its letters; TYPE straddles the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a class of things and a type of thing are the same grouping by shared features.

clue.text: Work out shoe strength

parts.note: a pump is a light shoe, such as a plimsoll or court shoe
iron = strength, as in an iron will

explanation.surface: Choosing shoes that give strength for a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' could be solve, but it is the gym sense; a pump is a British word for a plimsoll or flat shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump iron is to lift weights, a kind of workout.

clue.text: Feel aggrieved at being taken in by a media host

parts.note: per = a, each, as in 'ten pence a (per) go'
to resent is to feel aggrieved at

explanation.surface: Resentment at being fooled by a television host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is the hardest piece: it means each, so it gives PER, and 'taken in' pretends to mean deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter hosts a radio or television programme.

clue.text: Look again at compensation involving advert

indicators.note: compensation involves the advert, taking it inside

parts.note: redress is compensation for a wrong
ad, short for advertisement

explanation.surface: Reconsidering a payout that involves an advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look again at' means consider afresh, not physically look; readdress a problem is to tackle it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Address means deal with or consider, so the RE- prefix gives considering an issue a second time.

clue.text: Following drug in drink come down in imaginary world

indicators.note: the word for come down is following, so it is written after the drink
the drug goes in the drink

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of whisky
E, slang for the drug ecstasy
to land is to come down, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: Coming down after a spiked drink into a fantasy world.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a drug trip, and 'come down' is the landing, not the after-effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the land of dreams is an unreal place that exists only in the mind, often said of someone out of touch.

clue.text: Island not entirely in a former region of Africa

indicators.note: IN is not given entirely, losing its last letter

parts.note: Rhodes, a Greek island
IN without its N
A is used as itself

explanation.surface: An island partly situated in an African area of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a linking word placing the island, but it is fodder that loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the colonial name of what are now Zambia and Zimbabwe.

clue.text: One's son on St David's day is noble

indicators.note: one's son comes on, placed after, St David's day

parts.note: 1 March, the feast of St David, patron saint of Wales, written March I
one's, used as itself
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son born on St David's Day turning out to be an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: St David's Day, the national day of Wales, is 1 March, and the 1 is written as the Roman I. The pieces come in reverse of clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a noblewoman, the wife of a marquess or holding that rank herself.

clue.text: Fur rug concealing broken rusk

indicators.note: the rug hides the other letters inside it
RUSK is broken into a new order

parts.note: a mat is a small rug
RUSK rearranged

explanation.surface: A fur rug hiding crumbs of a broken biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fur rug' reads as one item, but fur is the definition and rug alone gives MAT. A rusk is a hard dry biscuit given to teething babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Muskrat is the fur of the muskrat, a North American water rodent, sold as musquash.

clue.text: Appointed politician to look after energy

indicators.note: after means later in order, so the word for look is written after the word for energy

parts.note: life = energy, liveliness
to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A politician appointed to take charge of energy policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as take care of, but look is PEER and after only sets the order. A life peer is appointed to Britain's House of Lords for life, the title dying with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Life peers are appointed, not elected or born, to sit in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Simpson possibly very good composer

parts.note: Bart Simpson of the cartoon, one possible Simpson
OK, fine, very good as a reply

explanation.surface: A Simpson who might be a fine composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' warns that BART is one Simpson among several.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer of the 20th century.

clue.text: Earthy reds at first aren't drunk

definitions.note: Terran here is the adjective, of the Earth; in science fiction it is also a noun for an Earthling.

indicators.note: the letters stagger into a new order
take the first letter of reds

parts.note: first letter of reds
anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.surface: Earthy red wines are not drunk at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earthy' and 'reds' suggest wine tasting, but earthy means of the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Terran means belonging to the planet Earth, a word common in science fiction.

clue.text: Brook, perhaps main source of water

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate, to stand
a water main is one kind of pipe

explanation.surface: A brook as the chief water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brook' looks like a stream, the obvious source of water, but it is the verb, to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpipe is a vertical pipe with a tap in the street, used for water when household supplies are cut off.

clue.text: Become united according to law but without support

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters for support are taken out of the legal word

parts.note: legally = according to law
a leg supports a table; removed

explanation.surface: Two sides joining forces legally but with nobody backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become united' sounds like marriage, which fits 'according to law', but it means form an alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to join together, become united in an alliance.

clue.text: Innocent child covered in gateau in US picnic party

indicators.note: the lamb is covered in cake, sitting inside it

parts.note: a gateau is a rich cake
a lamb is a meek, innocent person, often a child

explanation.surface: A little one smeared in cake at an American picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a messy toddler; the child is a lamb, a standard figure of innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is an American beach party where clams and other food are baked.

clue.text: Just show blonde straight up
Loose shark is swimming both sides of current

indicators.note: the shark's letters swim into a new order
the jumbled SHARK sits on both sides of I

parts.note: anagram fodder, 5 letters
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A shark has broken free and is swimming along either edge of an ocean current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like the escaped shark but is the definition, meaning dissolute. The jumbled SHARK splits as RAK and SH around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish means dashing and dissolute, like a rake, a loose-living man.

clue.text: Chaotic system of odd alternative technology vehicle

parts.note: strange = odd
AT, alternative technology, such as wind or solar power
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A muddled system for some eccentric green-powered vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a failed eco-invention; the answer is a term from chaos theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A strange attractor is the fractal pattern that a chaotic system settles into over time in chaos theory.

clue.text: Artist I note put in brown

indicators.note: I and the note are put in the brown

parts.note: tan = light brown
I is used as itself
ti (or te), a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A painter adding a note of his own to a brown canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also a colour, the auburn red named after the painter's favourite hair shade, which suits the brown wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a leading painter of 16th-century Venice.

clue.text: Concertgoer has to back replacing a male Evangelist

parts.note: a prommer goes to the Proms, the London summer concerts
TO written backwards
M for male; one of PROMMER's two Ms is the one swapped out

explanation.surface: A concertgoer has to support a male preacher who replaces another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evangelist' looks like one of the four gospel writers, but it is anyone who zealously promotes a cause. The Proms are an annual BBC concert season in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended sense: beyond the gospel writers, an evangelist is anyone who campaigns zealously for a product or cause.

clue.text: Sort of leather from gulls and relatives

parts.note: to gull someone is to fool them, to kid them
kin = relatives

explanation.surface: Leather made from seagulls and their relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulls' pretends to be the seabirds, which makes a comic leather; it is the verb, to fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidskin is soft leather made from young goats' skin.
